observed_evidence: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on September 23 that the United States and China agreed to extend the Busan Agreement until January 10 after his meeting with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng ahead of the Trump-Xi summit. Reuters reported the statement. No broader summit outcome or new semiconductor/export-control arrangement was verified in this event.
semantic_interpretation: The extension lowers near-term U.S.-China tariff/trade escalation risk and supports Asia/Taiwan external-demand visibility at the margin, but it is temporary and does not resolve Taiwan, technology export-control, AI or critical-mineral disputes.
